newsitem.title: GERMANY: Oil World sees weakening lauric oil premiums.
newsitem.headline: Oil World sees weakening lauric oil premiums.

text.p: Premiums for coconut and palm kernel oil over other vegetable oils are likely to weaken in May-September, the Oil World newsletter said on Tuesday.
The independent publication cited higher supply arising from improved crop prospects in key producer countries.
Coconut prices were at their lowest levels in 15 months and a further decline was possible, it said.
Oil World pegged combined global output of the lauric oils -- copra and palm kernel -- at 10.3 million tonnes in 1997, up by 800,000 tonnes from 1996.
Copra yields in the Philippines were likely to rise as a result of rains 13-14 months ago.
Indonesia was also anticipating a rise in the mature area under palm and coconut, which would bring higher output, Oil World said.
Encouraged by high world market prices, the country was favouring coconut oil exports at the expense of palm oil, which was increasingly used in the domestic market.
Lauric oil stocks were rising and offtake from the oleochemical industry was low, releasing more oil for food use, Oil World noted.
